To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
financial officers, financial auditors and analysts in Brazil and Europe have similar perceptions of the role of accounting in the economic environment.

(1) in both countries, the people interviewed consider that accounting information plays a role in capital market transactions, although the role is not the same; (2) the people interviewed consider IFRS to be more important in Brazil than in Europe; (3) there are significant differences between the people interviewed in Brazil and Europe in terms of their perceptions of IFRS; and (4) the differences in perceptions between Brazil and Europe are greater than those between auditors and financial officers or
financial officers in Brazil and Europe believe that accounting information is a key factor for the decision making process of investors, and that the use of IFRS will help fulfill this purpose.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how financial information can be used to make economic decisions in different environments and whether IFRS can be used to help fulfill the economic role of accounting information.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the role of accounting is to provide financial information that is useful in decision making, and that IFRS is an important factor that contributes to the usefulness of this information.
the role of accounting in Brazil has been more important than in Europe, but the role of accounting is still not very important in both countries.
, in Brazil, accounting information is not used to the extent it should be used, and that the IFRS will not change this situation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
accounting information is not considered to have an important role in the Brazilian economy.

the role of accounting is considered by all groups as a way to provide information to external parties, mainly to investors, and that the main role of IFRS is to provide a common framework for financial reporting, but that IFRS do not necessarily lead to more transparent financial statements.

the role of accounting is perceived as being more significant in the European context than in the Brazilian context, and that IFRS are perceived to be a more important factor in Brazil than in Europe.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the accounting process has a more important role in a developed capital market than in a less developed capital.

the role of accounting in an economic environment characterized by a well-developed capital market is to provide information for the efficient allocation of financial resources and that this role is more important in Brazil than it is in Europe.
the role of accounting in the capital market environment is perceived differently by the various groups of respondents.
